oliver.g: hi team, I'm day 1 and trying to scope Vault access for a feature spike. Do I ask for read-only keys or request full write access? Also unclear how KMS wrapping fits for sharing with partner sandboxes.

rachael.b: welcome! :wave: short guidance: prefer read-only user access for interactive work. If your job needs to update secrets (e.g., rotate test creds), request a short write window with a clear justification and duration. For sharing outside org use KMS wrap; we prefer giving partners a wrapped ciphertext rather than raw secrets.

matt.k: extra nuance: there are three common flows: 1) user read-only token (hours) for debugging, 2) temporary write window (explicit approval + audit), 3) service-role for long-lived programmatic access (auto-rotation). Avoid requesting write unless you truly need it.

oliver.g: how do I format the request? I saw other templates but want to include that it's read-only.

secrets-bot: Use: `@secrets-bot request env=staging resource=secret/data/team/<team>/<name> access=read|write reason="<why>" duration_hours=2 wrap_key=<kms_path> target_account=<acct> audit_label=<label>` Example: `@secrets-bot request env=staging resource=secret/data/team/redwood-inference/feature-spike access=read reason="local debug webhook" duration_hours=3 audit_label=onboard-oliver`

rachael.b: note the new `audit_label` field — it tags the request for automated reviewers and ties alerts to your ticket. Also add `sensitivity=high` if it touches PII or payment data.

matt.k: ops tip: when you need a partner sandbox, ask for `wrap_key` and `target_account`. We produce a KMS-wrapped ciphertext and a short README in the ticket explaining unwrap steps for common clouds. That avoids granting the partner any Vault access.

oliver.g: submitted: `@secrets-bot request env=staging resource=secret/data/team/redwood-inference/feature-spike access=read reason="test webhook and integration" duration_hours=4 audit_label=onboard-oliver`

secrets-bot: Request received. Ticket SEC-6153 created. Reviewer queue: infra -> eng-security. Expect ~20-40m. If you need write access later, reply with `upgrade=write` and include justification.

rachael.b: when you get a token, we authenticate via SSO OIDC. Run `vault login -method=oidc role=redwood-dev` after SSO popup. For local dev avoid persisting tokens: we recommend direnv or the secrets helper that injects creds into env for the session.

oliver.g: good to know. Also, does the scanning system look for PRs that reference secrets? I plan to add a test config; don't want false positives.

auditor-bot: Reminder: Any PR containing a reference to `secret/data/` must include `SEC-<ticket>` in the description. We run automated scanning and will block merging if a plaintext secret is detected. Use the secret-ref helper to fetch values at runtime instead of checking them in.

matt.k: local dev pattern we recommend: store sample fixtures with placeholder values in repo, and fetch real secrets at test runtime via the CI pipeline or local helper. For CI jobs we inject ephemeral tokens into pipeline env vars; never store KMS unwrapped plaintext in artifacts.

oliver.g: SEC-6153 approved, got read token and able to fetch secret. One more Q: what happens if I accidentally request write and it's approved? Is there an easy way to revert?

rachael.b: approved write windows are time-limited; if you need an early revoke open the ticket and ask for revoke. Infra will issue a revoke and re-issue minimal read tokens if needed. All approvals and revokes are audited. For anything touching prod we need two approvers and a revocation runbook.

matt.k: also FYI: we have a small pairing session for new hires tomorrow at 10am where we demo request flows and unwrap steps. DM me if you want an invite.

oliver.g: thanks all! joining the pairing session. closing this thread once I've updated my PR with SEC-6153. :thumbsup:
